title: Thread Count
description_html:
There are service_nodes micro-services in a system with bidirectional connections forming a tree, where the ith edge connects micro-services service_from[i] and service_to[i]. Each micro-service is configured with a maximum number of live threads; the ith micro-service can have a maximum of threads[i] threads.

The micro-services adjacent to each other must have maximum threads differing by exactly 1. Some configurations were lost; only k of the micro-services are known. This information is given as a 2D array currentValues of size k × 2 where each row is [micro-service index, maximum threads].

Find the maximum number of live threads each micro-service can have such that the total number of live threads in the system is the minimum possible. Return an array of length service_nodes where the ith element denotes the maximum number of live threads for the ith micro-service.

Note: It is guaranteed that the solution always exists.

Example

Given service_nodes = 5, service_from = [1, 2, 3, 4], service_to = [2, 3, 4, 5], k = 2, currentValues = [[1, 3], [5, 3]]:

1:3 — 2 — 3 — 4 — 5:3

There are 5 micro-services connected as (1, 2), (2, 3), (3, 4), (4, 5). Two known configurations: nodes 1 and 5, both with value 3.

The full list of maximum threads is [3, 2, 1, 2, 3]. These give the minimum overall threads with the adjacency-differs-by-exactly-1 constraint.

Function Description

Complete the function getMinSumNodeValues in the editor below.

getMinSumNodeValues has the following parameters:

  • int service_nodes: the number of micro-services in the system
  • int service_from[service_nodes - 1]: one end of the edges
  • int service_to[service_nodes - 1]: the other end of the edges
  • int k: number of known configurations
  • int currentValues[k][2]: the [micro-service index, maximum threads] pairs

Returns

int[service_nodes]: the configuration of the micro-services with the minimum possible live threads overall

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ service_nodes ≤ 105

Approach hint

Adjacent values differ by exactly 1 ⇒ the tree is bipartite by value parity. For each node u, the minimum feasible value is max(1, maxv ∈ known(val[v] − dist(u, v))) — essentially a multi-source BFS on the tree where each known node propagates (value − distance). Pattern: see LC 542 (01 Matrix), LC 2858 (Min Edge Reversals).
